PullRequest.Title: Improve customization message UI and migration behavior
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request enhances the customization messages and migration functionality in the chat feature. Key changes include:

- **Distinguishing Customizations**: The migration message now specifies the number of workspace and user customizations separately, e.g., "Found 2 workspace and 2 user customizations..."
- **Improved Navigation**: Clicking on "Review customizations" now directs users to the migration page and focuses on the first actionable control.


The implementation ensures that existing behaviors remain intact while enhancing user experience and clarity in customization management. All relevant tests have been updated and passed successfully.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send an Agent Host chat request while customization migration hints are enabled (once or always).
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The request model is shown first, then hint collection runs in Promise.all with hooks and automatic instructions; all three must settle before context is merged and the agent invocation proceeds. The diff changes hint metadata/count formatting and propagates the request cancellation token, but does not add a new awaited operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover workspace and user agent, instruction, prompt, and skill files through IPromptsService.listPromptFiles.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Six logical list invocations per hint computation across four unique prompt types; the prompts-service promise cache coalesces duplicate agent and instruction reads by type, so a cold run performs at most one discovery per unique type and warm runs reuse those promises until invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same migration computations and listPromptFiles calls already ran for each eligible hint; the diff only supplies the existing request cancellation token instead of CancellationToken.None.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery is part of computeMigrationHint and therefore part of the pre-agent Promise.all critical path when the experimental hint mode is enabled.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve and assess MCP server support for the active Copilot CLI session scope, including waiting for initial local MCP server loading and configuration resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One ref-counted support scope acquisition per hint computation, keyed by session type and normalized roots; concurrent holders share a scope, while an unshared scope is released after the snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same MCP scope acquisition and awaited assessment were already part of every eligible hint computation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial support snapshot is awaited by computeMigrationHint before the agent request can proceed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of discovered customization files and configured MCP servers. New work is two linear filters plus one combined candidates array over the already-produced migration candidates; boundary cardinality and concurrency are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Four migration computations run concurrently. Prompt discovery duplicates coalesce by prompt type through cachedFileLocations; MCP support is shared by scope key when another holder exists. There is no new unbounded concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt lists are cached as promises per type and invalidated by locator/provider change events, covering both cold coalescing and warm reads. MCP support is ref-counted rather than permanently cached. The diff does not change cache keys or invalidation; cancellation can stop cold discovery sooner.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the critical path and boundaries are real, and high confidence that their call count is unchanged by this diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Candidate counts are normally small, and no repository evidence establishes a user-visible cost from the added linear count formatting. Exact cold discovery and MCP assessment duration varies by workspace and server inventory.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the only added per-request work is bounded in-memory aggregation over existing results, while cancellation propagation can reduce abandoned work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Click “Review customizations” for a file-migration hint and open the first actionable migration category.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command awaits opening the singleton management editor, then awaits showCustomizationMigrationPage, which refreshes migration candidates before selecting and rendering the first non-empty enabled category.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover prompt files for enabled migration categories during refreshCustomizationMigrationInfo.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One refresh is explicitly added after open. A newly created editor already starts migration refreshes; overlapping listPromptFiles calls coalesce by prompt type, and an already-open editor uses warm cached lists unless an invalidation occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The review link opened the same management editor without selecting a migration page; editor creation already initiated migration discovery in the background.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The explicit refresh is awaited before the migration page is selected, ensuring the first actionable category is current.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize the MCP management widget and request the MCP gallery manifest/refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One widget initialization per newly created management editor pane; asynchronous manifest and refresh requests are initiated once by the constructor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same command already opened the editor, whose content eagerly constructs McpListWidget regardless of selected section.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The requests are fire-and-forget from widget construction and are not awaited by showCustomizationMigrationPage.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Enabled migration categories (default one, maximum three), unique prompt types, and candidate count. The added refresh repeats bounded provider enumeration, while filesystem discovery is coalesced by the per-type promise cache.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Enabled category computations use Promise.all; duplicate prompt-type discovery is coalesced. Refresh sequencing discards stale results but does not cancel older in-memory provider enumeration.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold editor creation populates per-type prompt-list promises; the newly awaited refresh shares or reuses those promises. Warm editor navigation reuses cached lists. Change events invalidate the relevant prompt-type cache before a later refresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that one refresh call is newly added and that prompt discovery is cached/coalesced; high confidence that remaining repeated provider work is bounded enumeration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: There may be uncommon providers with slower source-folder enumeration, but the concrete Agent Host providers inspected enumerate existing in-memory customization/source-folder state. No added uncoalesced filesystem or network fan-out was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the refresh is required to choose a current actionable category, its expensive file discovery is coalesced, and the remaining repeated work lacks a concrete user-visible performance mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Click “Review customizations” when the hint targets unsupported MCP servers.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command opens the same singleton management editor and synchronously selects the MCP Servers section after openEditor resolves; no new migration refresh is awaited for this target.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load MCP gallery manifest and refresh installed/gallery server presentation in McpListWidget.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One eager widget initialization per newly created editor pane, independent of which section is selected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior generic review command opened the same editor and therefore performed the same eager MCP widget initialization; the diff only directs focus to that already-created section.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initialization starts during editor construction but its manifest/refresh promises are not awaited by section selection.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed MCP server count and gallery results; the diff does not increase either boundary call cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Widget refresh and manifest loading remain asynchronous and internally owned by the existing widget; the changed section selection adds no burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The editor input is singleton-style, so reopening an existing pane reuses it. Gallery/service caching remains unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that section targeting does not add the MCP widget boundary because the widget is already eagerly constructed on generic editor open.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network latency and gallery size vary, but the relevant calls are pre-existing on the same editor-open path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the changed navigation does not introduce or amplify the expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 13 changed files and traced chat hint generation plus both review-navigation targets. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced; boundary counts are unchanged or coalesced, and added work is bounded metadata aggregation or cached refresh work.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
